comment: One weapon per hull kind. Speeds are units per tick (256 units = 1 m, 20 ticks = 1 s): 3840 = 300 m/s. Range is in metres and decides how long a shot lives - life = range / speed, so a shot that misses simply runs out of flight rather than being deleted by a special case. hitsAir/hitsSurface classify by KIND, not by altitude: a Manta is air whether it is at cruise or on the deck. ordnancePerRound is what one round costs out of the carrier's ordnance store when the hull is rearmed: a Manta missile is expensive, a gun round is not.

manta.comment: Guided air-to-anything missiles. Four aboard, and rearming costs ordnance out of the carrier's store, so a strike is a decision rather than a stream.

walrus.comment: A surface gun. It cannot elevate onto aircraft, which is what makes a lone Walrus ashore worth escorting.

lighter.comment: Unarmed. The logistics boat is a target, and protecting it is the point.

carrier.comment: Point defence, not an offensive battery: short-ranged and fast-firing. 600 rounds in the ready magazine, fed from the ship's ordnance store at reloadRoundsPer100Ticks - run the store dry and the ship is a target, which is what makes the depot run matter.
